short_description: Query - ODS Code usage within system
description:
Dear Support

I am contacting you hoping you can help with a query regarding your usage of ODS Codes, specifically the use of 'RW6' value that we include in our HL7 messages sent to your system.

An ODS code (also called an Organisation Code) is a unique code created by the Organisation Data Service. This code is used to identify organisations across health and social care.

Following the formation of Northern Care Alliance, the ODS Code 'RW6' for Pennine Acute Hospitals was legally closed by NHS England in 2022. NHS England have now confirmed that 'RW6' is going to be operationally closed at the end of September 2025. 

As such this email is part of our investigation into the usage and potential impact the operational closure of the 'RW6' code will have on all systems.

Although operationally and nationally this code will no longer exist we plan to continue to use it locally / internally as an identifier for what are the historic Pennine Acute Hospitals environments and systems and do not plan to change any existing inclusion in HL7 messaging unless it is identified that there is a need to do so. 

Current conclusions are that the continued usage of the 'RW6' code should only have a potential impact where it is being used on a wider scope external from each system, such as extracts, reports or inclusion in further downstream messaging etc.

To ensure there are no issues moving past the given date of September 2025 I am hoping you can answer the following questions

1)	Do you process the 'RW6' code sent in HL7 messages to your system?

-	it is typically included in the following HL7 fields but this is not inclusive of all systems and custom mappings:

                                                MSH:4
PID:3
PD1:4
                                                PV1:3
                                                PV1:6
PV1:9
PV1:17
MRG:1
LOC:1
OBR:4
DG1:3

2)	Do you storge the 'RW6' code within your system?

-	if so please identify as what and for what purpose.

3)	Do you use the 'RW6' code for anything within your system?

-	this could be hardcoded or included in a config setting

4)	Do you use the 'RW6' code for anything outside of your system?

for example 

o	Do you send the 'RW6' code to any other systems, databases etc.?

o	Do you include the 'RW6' code in any extracts, reports or datasets?

o	Do you include the 'RW6' code in any further downstream integration to other systems?

5)	Do you use or have link to the ODS Portal within your system (https://www.odsdatasearchandexport.nhs.uk/)?

-	if so what is this used for and is it automated to use the 'RW6' or other codes we send?

All help appreciated

Many thanks

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Jonathan Stanger-Moore
Senior Integration Specialist

Antivirus Exclusions: Confirm that the necessary exclusions are in place. I've attached an exclusions list—ask IT to verify that these are correctly configured.

Adjust Sophos Settings: If it works after disabling Sophos, request IT to disable the following settings before re-enabling Sophos:
Scan downloads in progress – Disabled
Block access to malicious websites – Disabled
Detect low-reputation files – Disabled

short_description: Process Expired Items Engine keeps failing
description: Since the beginning of this month (July),  the Event Engine control panel  has been frequently showing that the Process Expired Items engine is failing (see screenshot).  I have reported this before and was advised to report it if it happens again, which it has. While it occasionally shows that the process has been successful, more often than not, it will fail. I feel it is important for us to understand why this is happening and I also need re-assurances that if it is does fail, it will not then try and run again during the day time period.  Please advise.
assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 1 Team
close_notes:
Hi Gareth,
Good afternoon!

Your Full Daily Event Engine is triggered at 3 AM, as is your Expired Items Event Engine run. The recurring error pertains to deadlocks, which appear to be causing the Event Engine to fail. A deadlock on a database request has resulted in the failure of the Event Engine's expired run. Deadlocks are common and typically arise when multiple long-running transactions are executed concurrently within the same database transaction. We investigated the cause of the deadlock but could not identify any blockage at that time. We have also verified that there are no issues with the Expiry Candidate view (there are none). If this issue occurs frequently, we will need to conduct a more in-depth investigation to determine the root cause. However, since this is not a frequent occurrence, it should not pose a problem in your situation.

Kind regards,
swati

Uninstalling SSMS from the server will not impact the SQL Server database engine or the pharmacy application itself, as SSMS is not required for the application to run. However, removing SSMS will limit the ability to perform direct database management or diagnostics locally on the server. If SSMS is uninstalled, remote or alternative access methods would be needed for database administration.
If SSMS is outdated or causing issues, updating it is generally safe and recommended. If uninstallation is being considered, please ensure that alternative management tools or remote access methods are in place. We also suggest make sure there is latest a backup for the DB before you doing any changes. And try to update first on your UAT before rolling out to Live.

account: Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
short_description: Unable to specify time when prescribing PRN
description:
we have raised this issue before and it has been closed as it is considered system design, but we have now had an incident with a critical drug that has caused patient harm.

when prescribing PRN medications there are situations where it is crucial to be able to specify a time. Where possible, we use the dose rules to guide the administration as closely as possible.

For example, (scenario previously raised to Optum)
Zopiclone 7.5mg When required - you don't want the patient to take zopiclone in the morning, it is intended for sleep, but when prescribing PRN the system does not allow you to specify a time. The best you can do is to add dose rules of max 7.5mg in 24 hours, but that doesn't stop administration happening at any time of the day. Its also possible to add a start time to prevent the first dose being given before a certain time but that is too restrictive for a nurses drug round and will result in the patient not getting their medication at the correct time. 

New issue with critical medicine:
Patient is prescribed regular Co-Careldopa immediate release four times a day, a regular dose of Modified Release Co-careldopa at bedtime (22:00) as well as a PRN prescription for Co-careldopa immediate release at 22:00 alongside the MR IF the patient requires it, dependant on symptoms at that time. 
The prescriber specified in the notes that the dose was intended for 10pm but this note has no bearing on the prescription in ePMA and also isnt visible on the drug chart during administration unless the nurse clicks in to the prescription details therefore, the patient missed their 10pm PRN dose and was symptomatic throughout the night and wasn't given the PRN medication until 5am the next morning. This patient harm could have been prevented if it was possible to specify a time alongside PRN
assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 2 Team
close_notes:
Good Afternoon Fathima ,

I've been on a call with our Product and Clinical Safety teams to discuss your query, and this is the feedback we've come up with.

In our system, "When Required" prescriptions are designed to be ad hoc—they are not tied to specific times and are administered based on clinical need as it arises.

While the concept of "If Required" prescriptions (which are time-oriented but optional) is understood, this functionality is not currently available. However, we do have two workarounds that may help replicate this behaviour:

1) Prescribe as Once Daily at 22:00 with Directional Text
You can prescribe the medication as a once-daily dose at 22:00 and include direction text stating that it should only be given if the patient requires it. This will ensure the prescription appears on the Medicines Due For Ward desktop, allowing users to mark it as either Given or Not Given each day.

2) Use Directions or Notes to Guide Administration
Alternatively, you can use the Directions or Notes section to indicate that the medication is to be administered only if required at specific times. This approach allows the prescription to appear on the Drug Chart, providing clear guidance to clinical staff without enforcing a strict schedule. The prescription would always appear on the Medicines Due For Ward desktop under the PRN tab though. I've attached a screen-print of what this option looks like on the Drug Chart.

If you feel that native support for "If Required" prescriptions would be beneficial, you're welcome to submit an enhancement request via the following link:

https://emismedsman.ideas.aha.io/ideas/new

We appreciate your feedback and are always looking to improve the system based on user needs. If you'd like help implementing either workaround or have further questions, please don't hesitate to get in touch.

Kind regards,

Michael

account: Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
description:
Hi,

When printing a PAR, regardless of which option is chosen for the period, the entire PAR is displayed instead of just the requested period.

Could someone please look into this?

Steps
1/ Enter a patient record e.g 51030783
2/ Go to Drug Chart desktop
3/ Click PAR report on the Drug Chart tab
4/ Period - select 3 days
5/ Click View Report button

Expected Behaviour:
The report should display active prescriptions and the past 3 days’ administration records (based on the period selected).

Current Behaviour:
The report shows historical information from the start of the episode, regardless of the period chosen.

This is incorrect as it does not reflect the selected date range.

Not having a working PAR affects how we transfer information outside the trust. Providing more information than requested breaches data protection requirements, as it risks sharing unnecessary patient data.

Many thanks,
Hui
assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 1 Team
close_notes:
Hi Hui Yi Lee,

I understand the issue, however this looks to be as designed.

The report executes a Stored procedure on the database (called pPAR_Report_Detail).

Prescriptions are limited to the period because:
This SP states 'Only requests created since @StartDate are included' - the @StartDate is calculated by the CurrentDate minus 'Period' chosen.

Administrations displayed are then limited to Prescriptions that are within the 'period':
The SP states:
'--Now display Administrations/Problems for this prescription'

So the procedure first generates a list of Prescriptions within the period, then from that list - generates the administrations for those prescriptions, within the period.

Unfortunately we cannot alter the report, if you would like the functionality to change, please raise an enhancement request.
Or alternatively, you may be able to retrieve the information required from a BC report.

Kind regards,
swati

description:
Hello,

Hope you are well.

Situation:

We have been experiencing issues relating to the connection between EMIS and our BD automated dispensing robot (BD Rowa VMax)

When dispensing, EMIS is constantly stating that it has lost connection with the Rowa, and is not dispensing products.

The interface receives the stock quantity etc, but then goes to 'Connection lost to Rowa'

We currently have a job logged with BD, but I also wanted to check if there was an issue from the EMIS side.

According to my colleagues, this has been happening since Wednesday. I was alerted to this on Friday 29th Aug, as we experienced an issue with connectivity on this day, this was escalated to the robot supplier.

Over the weekend that has just gone, my colleagues informed me that the issue also occurred.

On the 01/09, we experienced another connectivity issue with the robot.

Later on on the 01/09 (around 5pm), the same issue surfaced.

Could this please be looked into ASAP?

Thanks,

Brad
assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 1 Team
close_notes:
Hi Bradley,

As far as we are aware BD fixed this issue with Pyxis version 1.3.

From our logs we can see multiple logs of ''Invalid HL7 message format ExternalOrderId is not unique'. Our product team took this to BD and BD advised this issue had been fixed in version 1.3 of pyxis. I would advise on speaking to BD to see if there has been any changes or other known causes for this error.

A contact ( Liam Clayton ) from BD have also stated the following, from conversations we have had with them :

'The robot requires all message received from a pharmacy system to have a unique order ID for traceability purposes; you want to be able to search for an order based on, for example, its picking ticket number, and find exactly that order. So any order it receives that has a duplicate order number will be rejected. What I have seen in the message logs is that EMIS has begun to reuse order numbers. Looks like it hit a cap of 99999 (or some number of 9s I can't nail down the exact figure) and then reset to 1. It's then gradually built back up to reach the number it was on when we first went live, and so the robot has started to reject the "duplicates" which have become more and more as the number has risen.

The solution : I've run a script on your database to archive all previously used order numbers. They're all still there for audit purposes , but now have order number + date + ARCHIVE. So if you search a specific order number in PIC you will still be able to easily find and identify it, but if that order number is reused it will now not reject it.

Future proofing - I will ask one of my more technical colleagues to set this script up to run automatically every 6 months or so and re-archive all new orders in the same way so that if EMIS restarts reusing numbers again we are covered.'

Please enquire with BD whether the same is required for yourselves.

Thanks,

Azeem

close_notes:
Hi Hannah ,

This issue has now been resolved.There was a misconfiguration within the PAR Report, so that the 'period' was being ignored.

Note :-if you looking for last 30 days.The report executes a Stored procedure on the database (called pPAR_Report_Detail).

-Prescriptions are limited to the period because:
This SP states 'Only requests created since @StartDate are included' - the @StartDate is calculated by the CurrentDate minus 'Period' chosen.
-Administrations displayed are then limited to Prescriptions that are within the 'period':
The SP states:
'--Now display Administrations/Problems for this prescription'

So the procedure first generates a list of Prescriptions within the period, then from that list - generates the administrations for those prescriptions, within the period.

Unfortunately we cannot alter the report, if you would like the functionality to change, please raise an enhancement request.
Or alternatively, you may be able to retrieve the information required from a BC report.

Kind regards,
swati

close_notes:
Hello Jane,

Upon reviewing order 222450 /221628 in the Stores Archive table, I can observe the status they held prior to the execution of the nightly archive job, which transfers them from the wOrder table. I can identify the two entries being archived by the overnight job. The entry from the 14th had a status of D (indicating Delete) and was archived that same day at 11 PM. The entry dated the 23rd is the one you received, thus it carries the status of R. Typically, when an order is deleted, it generates a Kind N transaction in the wOrderLog; however, this has not happened for this particular order.

This situation is part of a known issue that I had previously escalated to development. The manner in which the order was deleted without a type N line is as follows:

1) User A accessed the "Amend Orders to Suppliers" screen for the status 1 record.
2) User B opened the "Authorise orders" screen.
3) User B authorized the order, changing its status from 1 to 3. (This resulted in the Kind O transaction you are observing.)
4) User A pressed F6 to delete the order line; since this action was taken from the "Amend Orders to Suppliers" screen, it changed the status to D without generating a wOrderLog Kind N, as it presumes it is still a status 1 record.

The Product team has indicated that this would be considered an enhancement rather than a bug. To report it as such, please utilize the following form, and a representative from Product will reach out:

https://emismedsman.ideas.aha.io/ideas/new

In the interim, a workaround of creating a dummy order to facilitate receiving it can be employed. The Product team also mentioned that ideally, only one user should be viewing a supplier's order at any given time, ensuring that the user amending the order is the same individual authorizing it. This would help prevent the issue of users disrupting each other's workflows.

short_description: Where is the data from 'context audit viewer' desktop located in the server
description: Trying to pull the context audit viewer data, where can this be found in the raw data from database on the server 'mpft-ag-epma-p'
assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 1 Team
close_notes:
Hello Sara,
 
I'm pleased to let you know that we've found a resolution for your case CS1690579.
 
Thanks for adding me to the meeting. I have looked further into this regarding the GP Connect audit logs. It appears that GP Connect is not a desktop module; it is a service hosted by the API service. This is why it does not appear in the ContextAudit desktop, which only displays desktop?based context data.

There is some useful information available—such as request, response, and service details—in the tables Log_GPConnectAPIRequest, Log_GPConnectAPIResponse, etc., within the EMIS_GPConnectAPI database (a separate database). However, I'm not sure this aligns fully with your requirements, as I couldn't find any user or desktop details in these tables, nor any foreign key links to relate the audit data back to user information. I would suggest reviewing these tables to see if they help, but ensure you have access to the EMIS_GPConnectAPI database.

Alternatively, I have identified another potential workaround using the AuditLog table in the EHSC_HAP_LIVE database. You can filter by the table name 'ContextAudit' and data XML containing %ContextEvent="G"%. Below is an example query: Please test it by accessing GP Connect from different users and desktops and see if that reflects in the Audit log table.

SELECT TOP 1000 *
FROM icwsys.AuditLog
WHERE [Table] = 'ContextAudit'
  AND DataXML LIKE '%ContextEvent="G"%'
ORDER BY 1 DESC;
Make sure to apply date filters or use TOP 1000, as running a wide query may impact system performance. 

I would also recommend logging an enhancement request to have this feature permanently added to ePMA for clearer logging details. You can submit this using the following link.

https://emismedsman.ideas.aha.io/ideas/new

 
We're confident this will fully address the issue. However, if you find that the problem persists, simply click the red 'Reject Solution' button and we'll be happy to investigate further.

description:
Hi

When we try to us the barcode for product DVT428L (Short Chain Fatty Acid Enema Solution), it does not work (see screenshots).  the product barcode is 0735850820927  but in parts of Ascribe it scans it as 735850820927, omitting the first zero.

If we try to use the number 735850820927 in the item enquiry, it does not work.  We have tried adding it as an alternative barcode but it does not make any difference.  Please can you advise if there is a solution so that we can scan this product and the item enquiry function recognises it?

assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 1 Team
close_notes:
Hello Michael,

I am pleased to update we have found/come to a resolution for your case CS1694931.

Thankyou for your time on the phone today. 

As discussed the issue is your scanner is programmed to ignore the leading zero on a barcode.

This is the cause of the issue you are experiencing

"
When your 13-digit barcode starts with a '0', your scanner is most likely interpreting it as a 12-digit UPC-A barcode instead of a 13-digit EAN-13 barcode.
This happens because an EAN-13 barcode starting with zero has the exact same pattern of bars as its corresponding 12-digit UPC-A code. The scanner is typically configured to strip the leading '0' for UPC-A compatibility, resulting in a 12-digit output.

How to Fix the Leading Zero Issue
The solution is to change a setting in your scanner's configuration. You have a few main options:

Reconfigure the Scanner (The Best Solution)

You need to tell your scanner to handle EAN-13 barcodes correctly, which often involves scanning special configuration barcodes found in your scanner's user manual.
 * Enable EAN-13 Transmission: Look for a setting like "Enable EAN-13" or "Transmit EAN-13 as 13 digits."
 * Disable UPC-A Conversion: Look for an option that tells the scanner not to automatically convert EAN-13 codes starting with '0' into UPC-A codes, or an option like "Don't strip leading zero from EAN-13."
   * Manufacturer Example: For some scanners (like Honeywell), you would specifically look for the barcode to disable the automatic "UPC-A to EAN-13 Conversion" if it was incorrectly enabled, or enable a setting that ensures the EAN-13 is always transmitted as 13 digits. 

Application-Side Workaround (If Scanner Settings Can't Be Changed)
If you can't reconfigure the scanner or the host software, a less ideal but sometimes necessary fix is to adjust your application logic.
 * If the system searches for the scanned code and finds nothing, check if the scanned number is 12 digits long.
 * If it is, try searching again, but this time prefix the number with a '0'. This accounts for the scanner stripping the leading zero on valid EAN-13 codes.
Since reconfiguring the scanner is usually the cleanest fix, I recommend starting with its user manual and looking for the relevant configuration barcodes.
"

As mentioned I spoke with Northumbria who had the same issue. My advice was to liaise with the manufacturer and they would be able to advise on the scan codes required to allow the leading zero.

They did do this but due to the limitations on their scanners (they had a mix of Honeywell and Motorola scanners) this was not feasible. It was due to the limitations of the scanners they had.

Their workaround to this was - They had a barcode label generator which would print a barcode and they would put this over the barcode on the packaging and have this as the alternative barcode linked against the product.

Northumbria are now considering upgrading their hardware to new scanners to remedy this issue.

I would advise that you liaise with the Manufacturer for each brand of scanner you have and they would be able to advise if reprogramming your scanners would be feasible, this would also be the quickest and cheapest method if they can send you the scan codes.

Or the alternative would be to do as Northumbria has done above.

We are confident that this will resolve your issue, but if you find that this is not the case, please use the red 'Reject Solution' button so we are able to further investigate this issue for you.


Kind regards

Hello Bijan,
 
I'm pleased to let you know that we've found a resolution for your case CS1697585.
 
I have attached an excel document with the data you require to view - CS1697585.xlsx attached to this case

The script I used on the Live database was as follows

--
select consultant.entityid, person.forename as Forename, person.surname as Surname, consultant.gmccode, entityalias.Alias,
EntityLinkSpecialty.specialtyid, specialty.Detail as Specialty, consultant.out_of_use as In_Use from Consultant
join EntityLinkSpecialty on consultant.EntityID=EntityLinkSpecialty.EntityID
join specialty on EntityLinkSpecialty.SpecialtyID=specialty.SpecialtyID 
Join entityalias on consultant.EntityID=EntityAlias.EntityID
join person on consultant.EntityID=person.EntityID
order by 1
--

I was unable to have the have the wConsultantCodes  PasConsultantCodes in separate columns, but you can see the 2 codes grouped under each specific consultant


We're confident this will fully address the issue. However, if you find that the problem persists, simply click the red 'Reject Solution' button and we'll be happy to investigate further.

Hi Louis ,
Good Morning!

After conducting an investigation, I found that the issue was caused by a deadlock condition.

A deadlock occurs when two or more transactions become trapped in a circular wait, with each transaction holding a resource that another transaction requires and is waiting to be released, thus hindering their completion. For instance, Transaction A locks Row 1 and requires Row 2 (which is held by Transaction B), while Transaction B locks Row 2 and requires Row 1 (which is held by Transaction A). The database management system (DBMS) identifies this deadlock and usually resolves it by aborting (rolling back) one of the transactions, thereby allowing the other to continue.

This situation is not alarming as it has only occurred once.

Thanks,
swati

Hello Sue,

Thank you for the updated logs, these contain useful information.

Checking the audit log, you have multiple PCs starting up as comms. Unless you have barcode scanning enabled (unlikely as your comms log shows it disabled on computer L1827) you would need to disable comms on all but one of the following hosts:

[cid:image009.png@01DC7BDC.B1172D60]

Multiple comms will cause file locks with permission errors and other erratic behaviour. We can see evidence of this in your comms log with errors like 'Transaction no longer available' and 'Failed to save Transaction object' when trying to export invoices:

[cid:image010.png@01DC7BDC.B1172D60]

That is a non-standard configuration - PowerGate was not designed to have multiple comms PCs waking up to transact simultaneously.

This is likely the root cause of the issues you are seeing. Each PowerGate with comms enabled that either wakes up on a timer in minutes (interval) or manually by a user clicking the check local button (forced) will take over the import / export process. If another PowerGate does this at the same time, you will have conflicts.

PowerGate is designed to only have one instance with comms enabled waking up automatically (interval). Having so many comms enabled PowerGate PCs though, each with their own unique comms log, makes troubleshooting very difficult and hence is not a supported configuration.

If you want to try and make one PC the main comms enabled PowerGate server and turn the comms off on the others, this is something we can assist with (see attached guide).

Once you have ensured that you only have communications enabled on a single PowerGate PC, if the issue persists we can then continue to investigate the new instances to see if there are other problems.

Please test this on machine machine and advise if you do encounter any issues.

You helpfully provided the SQL code below to identify patients’ allergy records relating to Penicillamine from eMis.

 Can you advise which column(s) from those tables can be used to identify:

if the patient’s allergy record was deleted, and
what was the deleted date?
 

SQL code:

SELECT

p.Description as 'Allergy',

a.CreatedDate as 'Allergy recorded date',

ea.alias as 'Patient HospID'

Hello Andrew,

I am pleased to update we have found/come to a resolution for your case CS1722913.

If you would like an SSRS report creating for this by Optum you would need to liaise with your account manager
I have your account manager listed as Thomas Jennings - thomas.jennings@optum.com

Alternatively if you can create the report yourself this is the SQL script to generate the results in SQL 

open SSMS
Servername - HPFT-SQL-PROD02.nebula.xherts.nhs.uk
login in under windows authentication
New Query on the Live Database

you can use the following script

--

SELECT
p.Description as 'Allergy',
a.CreatedDate as 'Allergy recorded date',
ea.alias as 'Patient HospID'
FROM icwsys.DssAllergy A
JOIN icwsys.Product P ON A.ProductID = P.ProductID
JOIN icwsys.episode e on a.EpisodeID = e.episodeid
join icwsys.EntityAlias ea on e.EntityID = ea.EntityID
WHERE P.ProductID IN (
SELECT ProductID
FROM icwsys.Product
WHERE Description LIKE '%penicillamine%'
)
and ea.AliasGroupID = 22
ORDER BY A.CreatedDate

--

The results can then be place into Excel and you can manipulate the data that way.

account: Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
short_description: #940040 No error message when exceeding maximum PRN dose
description:
Hello Team,

We would like to re-open the investigation on case -CS1585092,

Firstly to explain more,

The issue identified is a silent failure within a safety?critical medication administration workflow, specifically when administering PRN variable?dose Controlled Drugs. When the nurse attempts to administer a dose that exceeds the configured maximum in 24 hours, the system:

1.briefly displays the loading indicator,

2.then returns to the administration window,

3.without showing any error message,

This behaviour shows that the system is running the validation, detecting that the dose is above the maximum, but failing to surface the required error message to the user. As a result, the user receives no feedback on why the administration did not complete.

This is the definition of a silent failure: the system rejects an action but provides no visible indication of the problem, no explanation, and no guided corrective action.

Why this cannot be considered an enhancement?

An enhancement is a request to add new functionality or improve an existing feature. This issue is not requesting new functionality. The system already contains the capability to check for maximum PRN doses and display warnings  demonstrated by the fact that:

1.Non?controlled PRNs correctly show warnings

2.Fixed?dose controlled drugs correctly show warnings

3.Only variable?dose controlled drugs fail to display the message

This inconsistency shows that the intended behaviour already exists, but it is not functioning correctly in a specific scenario.

Therefore, this is a broken workflow, not a missing feature.

Clinical safety implications

Silent failures in controlled drug administration pose a significant patient safety risk, because:

1.The nurse may assume the medication has been given

2.The nurse may repeatedly try the dose with no understanding of the cause

3.Workarounds may be attempted

4.There is no audit trail for the failed attempt

5.There is potential for dosing errors or breaches of controlled drug policies

Controlled Drugs require the highest levels of transparency, auditability, and safety messaging. A silent failure is unsafe and non?compliant with expected clinical safety and usability standards.

Conclusion:

Because the system is performing the validation, failing to display the validation result, and silently blocking a high?risk medication action,

this is unequivocally a defect in the error?handling logic, not an enhancement request. It requires a fix to restore the expected safety behaviour that already exists for other medications within the application.

Lastly ,we might need a meeting ,Please do investigate and let us know  the further actions ,

Thank you.

Best Regards,
Leela Kanaparthi
assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 2 Team
close_notes:
Hi,

Thank you for your further clarification.

You are correct that the system prevents RECORDING an administration when the dose is not due. The earlier statement referred specifically to this behaviour within EPMA, not to the wider clinical workflow outside the system. I appreciate the opportunity to clarify that distinction.

The workflow you describe — where the administration window can be opened for an early dose before the system applies the blocking logic — is the behaviour already documented within enhancement request MEDSMAN2?I?72. This was reviewed in 2022 by our Product and Clinical Safety teams and assessed as a Very Low Clinical Risk, on the basis that the system does not allow an out?of?schedule administration to be recorded.

As mentioned previously, resolving this requires new design and development work, which is why it has been scheduled as part of the EPMA modernisation programme. That delivery route remains unchanged, and all context you have provided has already been added to the enhancement record to support that future work.

As the item is fully logged, assessed, and planned for development within that programme, there is no further action we can take within the current product version. If any new information arises that would materially alter the original clinical risk assessment, we would be happy to review that through the standard safety?assessment process.

Kind regards,

Michael

assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 1 Team
close_notes:
Hello Jane,

Upon reviewing order 230631  in the Stores Archive table, I can observe the status they held prior to the execution of the nightly archive job, which transfers them from the wOrder table. I can identify the two entries being archived by the overnight job. The entry from the 14th had a status of D (indicating Delete) and was archived that same day at 11 PM. The entry dated the 23rd is the one you received, thus it carries the status of R. Typically, when an order is deleted, it generates a Kind N transaction in the wOrderLog; however, this has not happened for this particular order.

This situation is part of a known issue that I had previously escalated to development. The manner in which the order was deleted without a type N line is as follows:

1) User A accessed the "Amend Orders to Suppliers" screen for the status 1 record.
2) User B opened the "Authorise orders" screen.
3) User B authorized the order, changing its status from 1 to 3. (This resulted in the Kind O transaction you are observing.)
4) User A pressed F6 to delete the order line; since this action was taken from the "Amend Orders to Suppliers" screen, it changed the status to D without generating a wOrderLog Kind N, as it presumes it is still a status 1 record.

The Product team has indicated that this would be considered an enhancement rather than a bug. To report it as such, please utilize the following form, and a representative from Product will reach out:

https://emismedsman.ideas.aha.io/ideas/new

In the interim, a workaround of creating a dummy order to facilitate receiving it can be employed. The Product team also mentioned that ideally, only one user should be viewing a supplier's order at any given time, ensuring that the user amending the order is the same individual authorizing it. This would help prevent the issue of users disrupting each other's workflows.

Kind Regards,
swati

account: Norfolk And Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust
short_description: ePMA Crashing when accessing drug charts
description: On Sunday at roughly 18:30, we had users reporting issues with ePMA. The system was working fine until people accessed drug charts, it would then crash and stop responding. We restarted the SQL servers which resolved the issue. Could this please be investigated?
assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 1 Team
close_notes:
Hello Kieron,
 
I'm pleased to let you know that we've found a resolution for your case CS1731647.
 
ePMA uses "RequestLocks" to prevent two people editing the same drug chart at once. At around 18:30, a lock became stuck in the database, causing all subsequent lock requests to queue up and block each other. This resulted in drug charts freezing and ePMA becoming unresponsive. Restarting the SQL server cleared the stuck lock and restored normal service.
 
We're confident this will fully address the issue. However, if you find that the problem persists, simply click the red 'Reject Solution' button and we'll be happy to investigate further.
 
Kind regards,
Gunjan

Hello Baljit,

Thank you for raising your question regarding the use of the sysadmin role on the database server. We appreciate the concern you have expressed, and we understand why this level of access can be viewed as a potential security risk.

At this time, we would like to clarify that our application does not support a more granular database permission model beyond the sysadmin role.

Specifically:

The application requires sysadmin-level permissions on the database server to install, upgrade, and run correctly.
There is no supported mechanism to divide database permissions into smaller or least?privilege roles for application use.
We do not provide or support alternative configurations, such as using custom roles or restricting permissions to db_owner or feature?specific access.
This limitation is by design and not configurable through the application.

As a result, removing the sysadmin role or attempting to replace it with reduced database permissions is not supported and may lead to unexpected behaviour, failed upgrades, or application instability.

While we are unable to offer additional granularity within the database permissions themselves, customers typically mitigate associated risks through environmental and operational controls, such as:

Restricting access to the database server at the infrastructure or network level
Using dedicated service accounts rather than personal user accounts
Enabling appropriate auditing, logging, and monitoring
Limiting access strictly to authorised administrators

These measures help manage risk without altering the permissions required by the application.

Kind regards,

Michael

description: Our TIE will be down for 2 hours on the 24th of Feb 2026 from 08:00 to 10:00, this will cause a backlog of messages form the PAS, we plan to test the message throttling we have currently set for this, during that time, when the messages start to flow across the link again. we are currently set to 100p/m, we will slowly throttle up to  150 then 200 then 250, to see how the system copes. this is advance warning of the work we are planning, to make you aware that there will be down time and possible issues seen at those times.
assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 2 Team
close_notes:
Hi Stan.

The presence of a queue on the Pharmacy DB side is not inherently a sign of failure. Whether the queue accumulates on the TIE side or the Pharmacy side, the volume of work is the same — we're just seeing it in a different location. What actually matters is whether the Pharmacy service continues to process messages in order and without stopping.
If the oldest messages are still being worked on, the system is functioning correctly. A growing queue simply means the system is under increased load, not that it has stopped. The only scenario that would indicate a real issue is if the queue stops moving entirely — meaning the Pharmacy processing component has stalled and requires manual intervention. As long as messages are progressing, the system is working.

Example:

Imagine a shop with one counter and lots of customers walking in.

If customers arrive faster than the shop keeper can serve them, the queue grows.
But the shop keeper is still serving customers one at a time, continuously.
The length of the queue doesn't mean the shop keeper has stopped.
It means they're busy and still working through customers in order.

I appreciate that when viewing the Management Console it can be difficult to tell whether the rising queue is due to the service actually failing, or because messages are arriving faster than the system can process them. The way we do so in support is to go on the DB and do "select top 100 * from icwsys.InboundMessage". From there you can see what message is being worked on and what time it locked the message for it to be processed. We run the query, take note of the unique MessageGuid field, then run it again to ensure it has moved onto another message. As long as it does so no need to manually intervene.

Kind Regards,

Michael

Good Morning,

Please note that this SQL Agent job has failed for the last two nights on the same job step, due to becoming a deadlock victim.

Job name: EHSC_REPORT_LIVE - Overnight Job
Job step: Update rAMMPrescription

Failure Message:
pReport_Update_rAMMPrescription [SQLSTATE 01000] (Message 0)  Transaction (Process ID 178) was deadlocked on lock resources with another process and has been chosen as the deadlock victim. Rerun the transaction. [SQLSTATE 40001] (Error 1205).  The step failed.

Please can Optum advise if any further action is required.
assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 1 Team
close_notes:
Hi Kyle ,

I am pleased to update we have found/come to a resolution for your case CS1739846.

I have verified that all the jobs are running smoothly as anticipated with no failed jobs detected today. 

This deadlocked  issue happens when multiple transactions are interdependent, each waiting for the other to release resources, resulting in a circular dependency that halts their progress. This situation typically arises when one transaction locks a resource that another transaction requires, leading to a complete standstill. For instance, if Transaction A secures a resource while waiting for another, and Transaction B simultaneously locks that same resource while waiting for Transaction A, both transactions become blocked until one of them releases its lock.

We are confident that this will resolve your issue, but if you find that this is not the case, please use the red 'Reject Solution' button so we are able to further investigate this issue for you.

JOIN icwsys.episode e on a.EpisodeID = e.episodeid
join icwsys.EntityAlias ea on e.EntityID = ea.EntityID

close_notes:
Hello Emily,
 
I'm pleased to let you know that we've found a resolution for your case CS1752329.
 
I have reviewed the error logged during the Event Engine run: The error was,
"System.NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.
   at ICW.Model.EventsEngine.Services.RequestCreateService.<>c__DisplayClass3.<Process>b__0(Int32 i)"

This is a common technical error that occurs when the system attempts to read data that is not available at that exact moment (i.e., a value is unexpectedly null). This typically happens when a record is temporarily incomplete or in an intermediate state. Since the next scheduled run completed successfully, this confirms it was a transient data?state issue rather than a fault in the Event Engine. No further action is required unless this begins to occur consistently.

Regarding your second question about the difference between an Interval run and a Full run, the first difference is in the processes that are executed, which are listed below.

Interval Run :- 

Delete old administrations (if required)
Create new administrations
Process suspension notes
Process drug settings admin checks

Full Run :-

Delete old administrations (if required)
Delete home and self administrations
Create new administrations
Remove administrations with no results for deceased patients
Process suspension notes
Process drug settings admin checks

Behavioral difference:

The second difference is that the Drug Full Run triggers once per day and reviews all prescriptions on episodes within EPMA wards, generating doses for the next three days.
The Interval Run, however, is a smaller process that runs every 15 minutes and only looks at prescriptions created within the last hour on EPMA wards. This means the backend SQL limits the prescriptions it processes and generates fewer doses.
In your case, for this specific patient, it may not have been picked up by the Interval Runs because the prescription was likely created earlier than the one?hour window.


I hope this clarifies your queries. I will proceed to close this call for now, but please feel free to log a new case if you need any further assistance.

 
We're confident this will fully address the issue. However, if you find that the problem persists, simply click the red 'Reject Solution' button and we'll be happy to investigate further.

assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 1 Team
close_notes:
Hello Michelle,
 
I'm pleased to let you know that we've found a resolution for your case CS1771662.
 
I have looked into this example.
Quantity is calculated using the following approach:

For certain item types (LabelType = T, C, M), the system uses CivasAmount when it is populated
If CivasAmount = 0, it falls back to using Qty
For all other cases, Qty is used

Example:

Qty = 2 (2 vials issued)
CivasAmount = 1 (1 prepared dose)

In this case, the reported Quantity = 1, as the system prioritises CivasAmount when it is present.
I believe this is correct and working as designed.

Regarding the null consultant code on the report, I have checked and there are no consultant codes in the translog for those records where it is showing as null. The translog is pulled from Live through the overnight job. Please ensure that the consultant code is entered correctly in Live at the time of dispensing.

I hope the above information is helpful. If you feel that this is not the expected behaviour, the report may need to be amended. If you would like to proceed with this, please reach out to your Account Director so they can liaise with the appropriate team.

This job is scheduled to run daily at 02:00 and typically takes around 15–30 minutes. It should be absolutely fine for this database to be offline for up to an hour, as it does not affect live performance. In the worst?case scenario, standalone users may not receive the most up?to?date data if the database is offline during the scheduled overnight run.

Hello Rachel,

I am pleased to update we have found/come to a resolution for your case CS1779651.

Thank you for your time on the phone today.

As we found together this is now working correctly once the Robot files were installed on the affected machines.

As discussed

Each machine you perform and upgrade on or it is a new machine the robot files will need to be installed at the end of your upgrade process to ensure that machine can talk to the robot.

the process for this was as follows

"
Register ipport40.ocx:
Copy the file into c:\ascribe\smartclient

From the windows Start Icon run - Regsvr32 "c:\ascribe\smartclient\ipport40.ocx"

Register ascribeTcpipComms.exe
This is not part of the standard install package.

Copy the files into c:\ascribe\smartclient


open command prompt run as administrator
Type in the following - c:\ascribe\smartclient\ascribetcpipcomms.exe /regserver
"

If this is an existing asset and the name is not changing then the names should already be in the database waiting for the robot software on the machine to talk to the interface.

If this is a new asset and it is a new name then we will need to know the asset number as we did for 80402.

Once added and the robot files installed on the machine it began to work.

Going forward 

firstly ensure the robot files have been installed on the machine being upgraded or newly installed asset.

Then log a case with us requesting the asset is added to the robot interface.

The information we require when the case is being logged is 

Asset number - name of the terminal
Site number - location the terminal in

Once we have that the process is quite quick for us to add the asset into the interface.

If you know the asset numbers in advance for a new Machine then you can log the case before hand and the information will be in the database ready for once your upgrade or new installation is done. alternatively log them separately when you require them adding into the database

description: Hi, how can I get a list of all locations available on out Ascribe? I cannot get it from our reporting database. Please attached document. I want a list all locations with all the fields on the right.
assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 1 Team
close_notes:
Hello Bijan,
 
I'm pleased to let you know that we've found a resolution for your case CS1782797.
 

Please use the query below to retrieve ward details as shown in the Location Editor. Please note that we do not recommend running queries directly against the Live database, as this may impact system performance. Only use this if absolutely necessary.
-------------------------------------------------------------------
SELECT L.LocationID,LT.Description AS LocationType,WT.Description AS WardType,
W.Male,W.Female,W.SingleRooms,WG.Description AS WardGroup,RX.Description as 'RXTrackerWardGroup',
L.Description AS LocationName,L.Detail,W.out_of_use,L.ADAutoLogon,
MAX(CASE WHEN LA.AliasGroupID = 29 THEN LA.Alias END) AS WardCode,
MAX(CASE WHEN LA.AliasGroupID = 56 THEN LA.Alias END) AS PASCode

FROM Location L
JOIN LocationType LT ON LT.LocationTypeID = L.LocationTypeID
JOIN Ward W ON W.LocationID = L.LocationID
JOIN WardType WT ON WT.WardTypeID = W.WardTypeID
JOIN WardGroup WG ON WG.WardGroupID = W.WardGroupID
JOIN LocationAlias LA ON LA.LocationID = L.LocationID
left Join RxTrackerWardGroup RX on rx.RxTrackerWardGroupID =w.RxTrackerWardGroupID
WHERE LT.LocationTypeID IN (4)

GROUP BY L.LocationID,LT.Description,WT.Description,W.Male,W.Female,W.SingleRooms,
WG.Description,L.Description,L.Detail,W.out_of_use,L.ADAutoLogon,rx.Description;
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
We're confident this will fully address the issue. However, if you find that the problem persists, simply click the red 'Reject Solution' button and we'll be happy to investigate further.

Hi anne ,

To add them you would:

1) Go into the desktop "Editor - Consultant"
2) Enter their details and add their "PasConsultantCode" for instance "Name of consultant" has the code "eg. XX" .

Next this needs adding to the mapping of the "ITKADTPMI" interface.

3) To do this go to the desktop "PAS Management Console"
4) Use the drop down at the top to choose "ITKADTPMI".
5) Select the "Mapping Editor" tab
6) Press "Insert Mapping".
7) Use the drop down on "Mapping Group" to choose "The Consultant"; the From Code is what the PAS will send and the To Code is what we will convert that into. For example you already have "CHAPMM" for "From Code" and this goes to "MC" for the "To Code", so if the PAS sends to the pharmacy application "CHAPMM" as a consultant we would map this to "MC" which on "Editor - Consultant" belongs to "Chapman Dr Michael (Cardiology)".

short_description: Help with Access to Standalone TPN System
description:
We are currently experiencing an issue with accessing the standalone TPN computer system installed on the backup laptop (used in case of server failure) – EHSC Standalone 10.23
Bob (Robert Lucas) told us that we should be able to log into the OPTUM application using our “normal / live version passwords”. However, we have attempted all known credentials, including the system account, and none of them are working. As a result, we are unable to access the laptop and the TPN system.
Could you please assist us in resolving this issue or advise on how we can regain access?
assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 1 Team
close_notes:
Hello Anna,
 
I'm pleased to let you know that we've found a resolution for your case CS1797310.
 
To keep the Standalone system up to date, the laptop needs to remain powered on—especially at the scheduled time when the Task Scheduler job runs and completes.
You can check this by opening Task Scheduler (you can search for it in Windows). From there, you should be able to locate the scheduled job responsible for updating the Standalone system, note the scheduled run time, and ensure the laptop is turned on during that period.
Once the task has completed successfully, you should be able to log in using your current credentials, the same as those used in the Live system.
Your IT team, who set up the Standalone environment, should be familiar with this process. I would recommend reaching out to them so they can investigate further if needed.
 
We're confident this will fully address the issue. However, if you find that the problem persists, simply click the red 'Reject Solution' button and we'll be happy to investigate further.
 
Kind regards,
Muhammed Rashik
